details: The Trump administration has revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador to the US, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti, escalating a diplomatic feud. The move is in retaliation for Brazil's refusal to approve Trump's nominee for ambassador in Brasília and its earlier denial of visas to two US diplomats. Brazil has condemned the action, citing breaches of diplomatic norms, and the dispute is intertwined with Brazil's upcoming October election.
title: US Revokes Brazil Ambassador's Visa

details: Multiple US states, including Minnesota and Michigan, have reported cyberattacks on their water systems, causing operational disruptions but no reported contamination of drinking water. Federal officials suspect Iran is behind these attacks, which coincide with heightened tensions between the US and Iran. The FBI has launched an investigation, and cybersecurity agencies have urged utilities nationwide to strengthen their security measures.
title: US Water Facilities Hit by Cyberattacks; Iran Suspected

details: Iran's foreign ministry announced an agreement with Oman on the coordinates for a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz. This development comes amidst ongoing regional tensions and previous diplomatic efforts involving the US and Qatar to secure a deal for the vital waterway, which is crucial for global oil and gas transport.
title: Iran, Oman Agree on Strait of Hormuz Route

details: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reiterated that Israel will not withdraw from its current lines in Gaza until Hamas is completely disarmed. This statement was made following recent US-facilitated talks involving Israel and Lebanon aimed at broader regional stability. Hamas, in turn, has maintained that "resisting the occupation is its holy mission."
title: Netanyahu: No Gaza Withdrawal Without Hamas Disarmament
